1.title: GERMAN LESSON 1: Learn German for Beginners – German Greetings
1.focus: Watch once, then again while repeating each greeting aloud. Notice which greeting belongs to which time of day and which goodbye is formal.

questions.q: Anja says one goodbye is formal, for people you do not know very well. Which one?
questions.why: Auf Wiedersehen is the formal goodbye; Tschüss is for friends and family.

questions.q: Anja points out a pattern: “Guten Morgen, Guten Tag, Guten Abend” but “Gute Nacht”. Why?
o: Nacht is feminine; Morgen, Tag and Abend are masculine
Gute Nacht is only used in the south
questions.why: Masculine nouns take “Guten” (accusative), the feminine noun die Nacht takes “Gute”.

questions.q: Anja’s informal question for friends: “Hallo! Wie geht es ___?”
questions.why: Wie geht es dir? is the informal way to ask how someone is.

2.title: GERMAN PRONUNCIATION 1: The German Alphabet
2.focus: Say every letter out loud with Anja. Then spell your own first name and last name, exactly as she asks at the end.

questions.q: What homework does Anja give at the end of the video?
o: Spell your first and last name in German
Write a short email to a friend
questions.why: She asks you to learn the letters and spell your first and last name.

questions.q: Which German city does Anja spell in her exercise, after spelling her own name?
questions.why: She spells Berlin, the capital of Germany: B – E – R – L – I – N.

questions.q: For the letter E, what does Anja tell you to do with your mouth?
o: Pull it apart wide, like a smile
Round your lips into a circle
questions.why: The German E needs your mouth pulled apart.

3.title: Introduce yourself in German (for absolute beginners)
3.focus: Real people answer five basic questions. Listen for the question, then the answer, and repeat the answers aloud. Then answer the same five questions about yourself.

questions.q: Several people answer “Ich komme aus Berlin” or “Ich komme aus Zürich”. Which question are they answering?
Wo lebst du? – Ich ___ in Berlin. (wohnen)
questions.why: Both wohne and lebe appear in the video.

questions.q: A man answers “Ich bin Student.” Which question is this the answer to?
questions.why: Beruf = profession; Ich bin Student/Lehrer answers it.

4.title: GERMAN LESSON 19: EASY Conjugation of German REGULAR VERBS (+ Personal Pronouns)
4.focus: Follow the verb kommen through all pronouns: ich komme, du kommst, er/sie/es kommt … Then do Anja’s homework and conjugate wohnen yourself.

questions.q: Anja’s table: ich komme, du ___, er kommt.
According to Anja, how does the infinitive of about 99 % of German verbs end?
questions.why: kommen, wohnen, machen … remove -en and add the personal ending.

questions.q: Which verb does Anja give as homework to conjugate?
questions.why: ich wohne, du wohnst, er wohnt …

5.title: Counting in German from 1 – 100 (German Numbers for Beginners)
5.focus: Count along out loud. Notice the pattern for 13–19, the -zig endings for tens, and the surprising order in numbers like 37.

questions.q: Which numbers between 10 and 20 have no clear pattern, according to the video?
questions.why: elf and zwölf are special; 13–19 are built as number + zehn.
The unit comes first: sieben und dreißig.

6.title: GERMAN LESSON 23: The 6 Most IMPORTANT German Question Words!
6.focus: Learn the six W-words with their example questions. Write one question of your own for each word.

questions.q: Which question word asks about time? (Wann kommst du nach Hause?)
___ ist die Toilette? (Where is the toilet?)

questions.why: Anja’s example: Warum ist die Banane krumm?

7.title: GERMAN LESSON 9: The German Definite Articles DER, DIE, DAS
7.focus: Listen for the two big tips: always learn a noun with its article, and the -chen ending. Write down the six example nouns Anja gives.

questions.q: What is Anja’s most important tip for learning German nouns?
o: Learn every noun together with its article
questions.why: Always der Apfel, not just Apfel.

questions.q: Why is it “das Mädchen” although a girl is female?
o: Words ending in -chen are always neuter
Girls are grammatically neuter in every language
It is a mistake in the dictionary
questions.why: -chen makes a diminutive: das Mädchen, das Brötchen.

questions.q: Which article goes with “Frau” in Anja’s examples?
questions.why: die Frau, der Mann, das Kind.

8.title: How to Order in a German Restaurant
8.focus: Pick up the phrases in order: arriving, asking for the menu, ordering, asking for a recommendation. Practise the short waiter–guest dialogue aloud.

questions.q: How do you ask for a table for two people?
o: Haben Sie einen Tisch für zwei Personen?
Wo ist die Speisekarte für zwei?

questions.q: How do you politely order a red wine?
questions.why: Ich hätte gerne … = I would like …

9.title: “haben” and “sein” in the Past Tense (Präteritum Guide)
9.source: YouTube · Learn German with Herr Antrim
9.focus: Follow the conjugation tables for hatte and war, then read every example sentence aloud. Note which past tense he says Germans prefer for these two verbs.

questions.q: Which past tense do most Germans use in speech for haben and sein?
questions.why: For haben and sein the short Präteritum forms are the natural choice in speech.
ich war, du warst, er war …

questions.q: “As a child I ___ a lot of toys.” Which German form fits?

10.title: Learn German Vocabulary – Countries & Languages in German (Länder und Sprachen)
10.focus: Repeat each pair aloud (country, then language). Notice that most language names end in -isch. Make a note of the countries that come with an article.

questions.q: Which language do people speak in Österreich?
questions.why: Österreich – Deutsch, as in the video.

questions.q: Which of these country names comes with an article?
questions.why: die Türkei, die USA, die Schweiz.

11.title: GERMAN LESSON 15: The German indefinite articles EIN and EINE
11.focus: Sort each of Anja’s example nouns by gender. Do her mini exercise at the end (Stift, Flasche, Kissen, Kartoffeln) before she gives the solution.

questions.q: How many indefinite articles does German have (in the nominative)?
questions.why: ein for masculine and neuter, eine for feminine.

questions.q: Which indefinite article is used with plural nouns such as “Schuhe”?
questions.why: das sind Schuhe – no article in the plural.

12.title: How to Negate German Sentences – NICHT vs. KEIN for Beginners
12.focus: Watch how nicht changes position, then how kein replaces ein/eine. Make your own negated version of each example.

questions.why: With a plain verb, nicht comes after it.
With an adjective, nicht stands before it.

questions.q: Ich habe eine Tochter. → Ich habe ___ Tochter.

13.title: My new house! Learn German Vocabulary of Furniture and Rooms!
13.focus: Walk through Anja’s house room by room and write down each room and piece of furniture with its article. Her homework: write a few sentences about your own home.

questions.q: Anja explains “das Wohnzimmer”. Which two parts is it built from?
questions.why: The living room is the room to live in.
kühl = cool, der Schrank = cupboard: fridge.

questions.q: What is the plural of “das Fahrrad”, as Anja says?

14.title: LESSON 16: Learn the German POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS: Mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser …
14.focus: Write the list mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, ihr/Ihr next to the pronouns ich, du, er, sie … and watch which endings appear with feminine and plural nouns.

questions.why: sein = his (and also “to be”, as Anja jokes).

15.title: GERMAN LESSON 46: German Separable Verbs Explained – Trennbare Verben
15.focus: Notice how the prefix jumps to the end of the sentence. Say each of Anja’s examples aloud, then make two of your own with aufstehen and einkaufen.

questions.q: “Der Zug fährt um 9 Uhr ab.” Where does the prefix “ab” stand?
o: At the end of the sentence
questions.why: The prefix of a separable verb goes to the end in main clauses.

questions.q: What is the infinitive in “Der Zug fährt ab”?

o: Ich stehe auf um 7 Uhr früh dann.

16.title: Learn German Vocabulary – Hobbies in German (Hobbys)
16.focus: Repeat every hobby aloud and then say the two model sentences with your own hobbies.

questions.q: How do you say “My hobby is cooking”?
Which sentence is correct for two hobbies?
o: Meine Hobbys sind lesen und Musik hören.
Mein Hobbys ist lesen und Musik hören.

questions.q: How does the video say “Ski” in “Skifahren” should be pronounced at the start?

17.title: GERMAN LESSON 59: How to tell the TIME in German – Die Uhrzeit (part 1)
17.focus: Say every clock time out loud with Anja. Watch how she adds 12 to get the 24-hour time and how halb works.

questions.q: How do you ask what time it is?
questions.why: Also: Wie viel Uhr ist es?

questions.q: How does Anja say 4 pm in the 24-hour style?

questions.why: halb fünf – half of the way to five.

18.title: Learn German | German Grammar | Modalverben | Modal verbs | A1
18.focus: List the six modal verbs and note the structure: conjugated modal verb in position 2, infinitive at the very end.

questions.q: How many modal verbs are there in German?
questions.why: dürfen, können, mögen, müssen, sollen, wollen.

questions.q: In a sentence with a modal verb, where does the second verb (infinitive) go?

questions.why: ich kann, du kannst, er kann.

19.title: GERMAN LESSON 14: German professions – Deutsche Berufe: Was sind Sie von Beruf?
19.focus: Note the male and female forms of each job and say the jobs aloud. Then say what you do: “Ich bin …”.

questions.q: How do you formally ask someone’s profession?
What is the female form of “der Lehrer”?
How do you say “I am a teacher” (female)?
questions.why: Professions normally have no article after sein.

20.title: Learn German | German Grammar | Dative case | Dativ | A1
20.focus: Watch how the articles change in the dative and which question word finds the dative object. Pause and repeat each example sentence.

questions.q: Which question word asks for the dative object?
questions.why: Wem gebe ich das Buch? – dem Mann.

questions.q: Ich gebe ___ Mann das Buch. (der Mann, dative)
Which preposition always takes the dative?
questions.why: mit dem Bus, mit der Bahn.

21.title: How to Give Directions in German | Super Easy German 185
21.focus: Follow the route on the map while you listen. Collect every direction word: geradeaus, links, rechts, die Straße, die Ampel.

o: How do I get to the station?

22.title: An EASY explanation of the 9 Two-Way PREPOSITIONS (Wechselpräpositionen)
22.focus: Learn the nine prepositions, then the one trick: wo? = dative (position), wohin? = accusative (movement).

questions.q: How many two-way prepositions does German have?
questions.why: an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen.

questions.q: Which case follows a two-way preposition when you answer “Wohin?” (movement)?
Das Buch liegt auf ___ Tisch. (der Tisch, wo?)

23.title: GERMAN LESSON 27: Learn German Vocabulary of FOOD (Das Essen)
23.focus: Write each food word with its article. Repeat aloud and say which foods you like.

o: When you arrive at a hotel
questions.why: It is the wish for a good meal.

24.title: Hoch, höher am höchsten! (German Comparative)
24.focus: Note how the comparative ends in -er and the superlative in am … -sten, and which vowels get an umlaut.

25.title: Grocery shopping in German | Super Easy German (33)
25.focus: Listen to real shop conversations. Notice how people ask for quantities and how the shop assistant asks “Sonst noch etwas?”.

questions.q: Who usually says “Was darf es sein?”
questions.why: It means: What can I get you?

questions.q: “Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Äpfel.” means:
o: I would like a kilo of apples.
I have a kilo of apples.
questions.why: Ich hätte gern = I would like.

26.title: Imperatives: How to Phrase Orders and Requests in German
26.focus: Compare the three imperative forms (du, ihr, Sie) and the politeness words bitte and mal.

questions.why: Remove -st from the du-form: du kommst → Komm!

questions.q: What is the formal imperative of “kommen”?

27.title: Understand the German Perfect! (Only in German) – Das deutsche Perfekt
27.focus: Anja explains the Perfekt in German only. Listen for haben/sein and the Partizip II at the end of the sentence.

questions.why: Ich habe gegessen. Ich bin gefahren.

questions.q: Where does the Partizip II stand in a main clause?

28.title: Perfekt mit SEIN: When to use the German PERFECT Tense with “to Be”
28.focus: List the two groups of verbs that take sein: movement (gehen, fahren, fliegen) and change of state (aufwachen, werden), plus sein and bleiben.

questions.q: Which verbs typically form the Perfekt with sein?
o: Verbs of movement and change of state
questions.why: Ich bin gefahren, ich bin aufgewacht.

questions.q: What is the Partizip II of “gehen”?

29.title: Learn German Vocabulary – Weather in German (Wetter)
29.focus: Repeat each weather expression aloud, then say what the weather is like where you are today.

30.title: German Clothing Vocabulary
30.focus: Note the gender of every item of clothing, and which items are always plural (die Schuhe, die Socken, die Jeans).

questions.q: Which article goes with the plural “Schuhe”?

31.title: A1 – Lesson 25 | the family in German | die Familie | Meine Familie
31.focus: Build the family tree with the German words and say sentences: Das ist mein Bruder. Meine Mutter heißt …

questions.q: Meine Mutter und mein Vater sind meine ___. (parents)

32.title: The ACCUSATIVE Part 4: German MICH, DICH, EUCH, … Personal Pronouns of the accusative
32.focus: Write the full table: mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie/Sie. Then make one sentence for each.

questions.q: Which case are mich, dich, ihn, sie, es in?

33.title: Sports in Slow German
33.focus: Listen to the slow German and note the sports, the verbs (spielen, machen, gehen) and how often people exercise.

questions.q: How do you say “I play tennis”?

34.title: How Do Germans Stay in Shape? | Easy German 424
34.focus: Street interviews about sport and fitness. Turn on the German subtitles, and note how people answer “Machst du Sport?”.

questions.q: “Wie oft machst du Sport?” asks about:

35.title: A1 – Lesson 59 | Beim Arzt | At the Doctor’s | Arzttermin vereinbaren
35.focus: Follow the dialogues: making an appointment, describing pain, and the doctor’s advice. Repeat the key sentences.

o: I would like to make an appointment.
I would like to cancel my visit.

36.title: Don’t Mix Up “seit”, “für” & “vor”! (German Temporal Prepositions)
36.focus: Compare the three prepositions: seit (since, still going on), für (for a planned length), vor (ago).

questions.q: “Ich wohne seit zwei Jahren in Berlin.” means:
o: I have been living in Berlin for two years (and still do).
I lived in Berlin two years ago.
I will live in Berlin for two years.
questions.why: seit + dative + present tense = since/for until now.
seit einem Jahr = for a year now.

37.title: THE DATIVE part 3: Mir, dir, Ihnen in GERMAN – Personal Pronouns in the DATIVE
37.focus: Write the table mir, dir, ihm, ihr, ihm, uns, euch, ihnen, Ihnen and make a sentence with each.

questions.why: geben takes the dative for the person.

questions.q: What is the formal dative of “you”?

38.title: Subjunctive 2 with “hätten” & “wären” – 3 Minuten Deutsch #68
38.source: YouTube · Learn German with Herr Antrim
38.focus: Note how hätte and wäre express wishes and polite requests. Use them to finish the sentences: Ich hätte gern … Ich wäre gern …

questions.why: hätte gern = would like to have.

o: I would like to be rich.

questions.q: Ich ___ gern ein Haus. (haben, polite wish)

40.title: Seit oder Vor? | Since, for and ago explained | German Time Prepositions
40.focus: Note which tense goes with seit (present) and which with vor (Perfekt/Präteritum). Make one sentence of your own with each.

questions.q: “Ich wohne seit zwei Jahren in Berlin.” The person:

41.title: German Two-Part Conjunctions | Super Easy German 199
41.focus: Collect the pairs: entweder … oder, sowohl … als auch, weder … noch, nicht nur … sondern auch, zwar … aber. Write one example for each.

questions.why: Er spricht sowohl Deutsch als auch Englisch.
Ich habe weder Zeit noch Geld.

questions.q: Er ist ___ müde, aber er arbeitet weiter. (admittedly)

42.title: A2 – Lesson 3 | Konjunktion “dass” | Nebensatz
42.focus: Watch how the verb jumps to the end after dass, and practise turning two main clauses into one sentence with dass.

questions.q: Where does the conjugated verb stand in a dass-clause?

o: Sie sagt, dass sie müde ist.
Sie sagt, dass sie ist müde.
Sie sagt, dass ist sie müde.

43.title: A2 – Lesson 16 | Indirekte Fragesätze | ob
43.focus: Turn each direct question into an indirect one (Ich weiß nicht, wo … / ob …). Notice the verb at the end.

questions.q: A yes/no question becomes an indirect question with:
questions.why: Kommt er? → Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt.

questions.q: Ich möchte wissen, ___ du Zeit hast. (whether)

44.title: How to use “weil” EXPLAINED | Konjunktion WEIL erklärt | A2
44.focus: Focus on the verb at the end and on what happens when the weil-clause comes first in the sentence.

o: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich bin krank.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil bin ich krank.

questions.q: If the weil-clause comes first, the main clause starts with:
questions.why: Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause.

questions.q: Ich komme nicht, ___ ich arbeiten muss. (because)

45.title: Deutsch lernen A2: Wortschatz für die Bank (Konto eröffnen, EC Karte beantragen …)
45.focus: Collect the bank words (Konto, Girokarte, Überweisung, Kontoauszug) and practise one dialogue: “Ich möchte ein Konto eröffnen.”

46.title: Genders of German Nouns: Tips, Tricks & Memory Tools
46.source: YouTube · Learn German with Herr Antrim
46.focus: Write down the endings that always signal the article: -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -ion (die) and -chen, -lein (das).

47.title: Deutsch lernen - Geldautomat | Deutsch lernen mit Dialogen
47.focus: Listen to the dialogue and note the steps: Karte einstecken, PIN eingeben, Betrag wählen, Geld abheben. Then say the steps aloud.

48.title: How to Remember Possessive Article Endings
48.focus: Learn the trick: possessives take the same endings as ein/kein. Practise with mein-, dein-, unser- in all three cases.

questions.q: Possessive articles (mein, dein …) take the endings of:
questions.why: mein Vater, meine Mutter, meinem Vater.

questions.q: Which is the accusative of “mein Bruder”?

49.title: Learn German: adjective endings explained logically! Grammar A2–B2
49.focus: Notice the three tables (after der, after ein, without article). Decide the ending each time before the video shows it.

questions.q: After the definite article in the nominative masculine: “der ___ Mann”
After ein in the nominative masculine: “ein ___ Mann”
questions.why: ein großer Mann (er = the article’s missing ending).

50.title: 5 Meanings of the Verb “Sollen” | Super Easy German 198
50.focus: Sort the five meanings: order from others, advice, offers, reported rumours, and questions of doubt.

o: an offer / question about what to do
You are not supposed to lie.

questions.why: Du solltest … is the polite advice form.

51.title: Deutsch A2 Pflege-Wortschatz: 30 wichtige Wörter für den Pflegeberuf
51.focus: Learn the key care words (pflegen, der Pfleger, das Pflegeheim, der Patient) and say what you would need to do in a care job.

52.title: Deutsch lernen: Haushalt | Hausarbeit – Wortschatz
52.focus: Write down each chore verb with its noun (Wäsche waschen, Geschirr spülen, staubsaugen) and say which ones you do daily.

questions.q: Ich ___ jeden Tag das Geschirr. (spülen, ich)

53.title: Verben + Präpositionen | A2 B1 B2
53.focus: Copy the verb–preposition–case combinations into your notebook: warten auf + Akk., träumen von + Dat., denken an + Akk., sich interessieren für + Akk.

54.title: A2 – Lesson 42 | Ratschläge geben | sollte | Konjunktiv II
54.focus: Collect the advice patterns: Du solltest …, An deiner Stelle würde ich …, Ich würde dir raten, … Write three pieces of advice for a friend.

o: If I were you, I would …

questions.q: Ich ___ dir raten, das nicht zu tun. (would)

55.title: Als vs Wie? | Comparison in German
55.focus: Sort the sentences: als after a comparative, wie after so / genauso. Write two of each.

56.title: German for Beginners #39: und, oder, aber, denn, sondern
56.source: YouTube · Learn German with Herr Antrim
56.focus: Memorise the five conjunctions that do not change word order (ADUSO: aber, denn, und, sondern, oder).

questions.q: Which conjunction is used after a negation: “Ich bleibe nicht hier, … ich gehe.”

questions.why: denn does not change the word order.

57.title: German Hotel Vocabulary | Super Easy German 186
57.focus: List the reception phrases you would need: booking, key, breakfast, checking in and out, complaints.

questions.q: “Das Frühstück ist im Preis inbegriffen.” means:
o: Breakfast is included in the price.

58.title: 43 Words You Need for Traveling by Train in Germany | Super Easy German 224
58.focus: Note the essential words: Gleis, Abfahrt, Ankunft, Verspätung, umsteigen, Fahrkarte, Bahnsteig. Say each in a sentence.

questions.why: Der Zug fährt auf Gleis 7 ab.

59.title: How to buy a metro ticket in Berlin | Super Easy German (106)
59.focus: Follow the machine steps and note the words for ticket types (Einzelfahrschein, Tageskarte) and validating (entwerten).

questions.why: You stamp/validate it before the ride.

questions.q: Ich brauche eine ___ für den ganzen Tag. (day pass)

60.title: Reflexive Verben mit Akkusativ | German Reflexive Verbs Explained!
60.focus: Write the reflexive pronoun table and add five verbs you use daily (sich waschen, sich anziehen, sich freuen, sich treffen, sich setzen).

61.title: German Da-Words | Super Easy German (80)
61.focus: See how da(r)- replaces preposition + thing (damit, darauf, dafür) and wo(r)- asks about it (womit, worauf).

62.title: Adjektive mit Präpositionen – Welche Präposition ist richtig?
62.focus: Learn the pairs together: stolz auf, zufrieden mit, verliebt in, interessiert an, froh über. Test yourself covering the preposition.

63.title: B1 – Lesson 27 | Meinung sagen | express opinion
63.focus: Collect phrases for opinions, agreement and disagreement. You will need them for the speaking exam.

questions.q: Ich bin der Meinung, ___ das richtig ist. (that)

64.title: German Dative Case: 15 Simple Verbs That Always Take the Dative
64.focus: Learn the list: helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, schmecken, passen, gratulieren, zuhören, antworten, fehlen … and make one sentence for each.

65.title: How to Use German Indefinite Pronouns | Super Easy German 221
65.focus: Group the pronouns: persons (man, jemand, niemand, alle, jeder) and things (etwas, nichts, alles).

questions.q: In Deutschland isst ___ viel Brot. (one / people)

66.title: Reflexive pronouns in German – Accusative or Dative?
66.focus: Only ich and du change: mich/mir, dich/dir. Find out when a body part forces the dative (Ich wasche mir die Hände).

questions.why: body part = accusative object → reflexive in the dative.

questions.q: Du kaufst ___ ein neues Handy. (reflexive dative, du)

67.title: Is Volunteering Popular in Germany? | Easy German 471
67.focus: Street interviews. Listen for words like ehrenamtlich, das Ehrenamt, der Verein, sich engagieren, and note who volunteers where.

68.title: Important German temporal adverbs | nie, selten, manchmal, oft, immer & more
68.focus: Order the words on a scale from nie to immer and say how often you do five things.

questions.q: Which word means the highest frequency?
Ich gehe ___ ins Kino, nur einmal im Jahr. (rarely)

69.title: How to ask the perfect question in German
69.focus: Compare direct and polite indirect forms (Wo ist …? → Können Sie mir sagen, wo … ist?).

questions.q: “Können Sie mir sagen, wo der Bahnhof ___?”

o: Können Sie mir sagen, wie spät es ist?

70.title: Text like a German! (German Abbreviations)
70.focus: Note the abbreviations: LG, MfG, z. B., usw., ca., bzw., d. h. Say which ones you can use in an email to a friend and which in a formal email.

71.title: Telefongespräch auf Deutsch | Telefonat mit Kundenservice + Beschwerde
71.focus: Listen for the polite phrases: Ich möchte mich beschweren, Ich bin unzufrieden, Können Sie mir helfen? Repeat the dialogue aloud.

72.title: How to Build Longer German Sentences with Relative Clauses
72.focus: Build three sentences of your own: one for each gender. Underline the relative pronoun and circle the final verb.

questions.q: Das ist der Mann, ___ mir geholfen hat. (relative pronoun)
Das ist die Frau, ___ dort wohnt. (relative pronoun)
In a relative clause the conjugated verb goes:

73.title: Relative clauses: who, which, that explained simply!
73.focus: Compare the English who / which / that with der / die / das, and check the gender of your noun first.

questions.q: The relative pronoun agrees with the noun in:
questions.why: Gender and number decide, the case comes from the clause.

questions.q: Das Kind, ___ dort spielt, ist mein Neffe. (neuter)

74.title: Relativsatz German | Akkusativ | Relativpronomen im Akkusativ
74.focus: See that only the masculine changes (der → den) in the accusative. Make five sentences with the verb at the end.

questions.q: Das ist der Kuchen, ___ ich gebacken habe. (masculine accusative)
Das ist die Frau, ___ ich kenne. (feminine accusative)
Which relative pronoun changes in the accusative?

75.title: DW Deutsch lernen | Deutsch im Job | B1 | Gastronomie | Wissenscheck
75.focus: Listen for typical vocabulary in restaurants and catering. Do the quiz along with the video.

questions.q: “die Küche” in a restaurant job is:
Der Koch ___ das Essen zu. (zubereiten, er)

76.title: DTZ / Telc B1 Briefe schreiben | Einladung
76.focus: Note the structure of an invitation: Anrede, Anlass, Datum/Uhrzeit/Ort, Bitte um Antwort, Gruß. Write one invitation to a friend.

questions.q: Which greeting starts a letter to a friend?
Ich lade dich ___ meinem Geburtstag ein. (to)

77.title: Deutsch für B1/B2 #33: Gradpartikeln – Verstärkung
77.source: YouTube · Learn German with Herr Antrim
77.focus: Rank the intensifiers from weak to strong: ziemlich, sehr, äußerst, unglaublich, total. Use three of them in sentences about your week.
